heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini handles Overture PETG straight out of the box with its stock direct drive extruder and stainless steel nozzle, achieving a safe maximum print speed of 167 mm/s based on a 14 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. Because PETG requires no enclosed chamber and is non-abrasive, the open-frame setup paired with the 80°C bed limit provides reliable, clean results.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with glue stick or liquid release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent underextrusion during high-speed segments.
Enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' (Max Detour Length: 150 mm) to reduce visible stringing and travel wiping across outer perimeters.
Lower outer wall acceleration to 3000 mm/s² and outer wall speed to 100 mm/s to eliminate surface ringing and gloss inconsistency.
Set Z Hop type to 'Spiral' or 'Normal' with a height of 0.4 mm to prevent nozzle collision with curling PETG perimeters.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is hygroscopic and draws atmospheric moisture quickly, causing steam expulsion, oozing, and fine spiderweb stringing.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours in an active filament dryer, and increase retraction distance to 0.8 mm with 35 mm/s speed in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First Layer PEI Coating Delamination / Over-adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG bonds aggressively to raw PEI sheets via molecular adhesion, causing plate coating tear-out upon part removal.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin, even coat of PVP glue stick or liquid Bambu liquid glue as an interface release agent before printing, and wait for the bed to fully cool before releasing.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speeds chilling the extruded track below thermal bonding temperature.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Cap the part cooling fan maximum to 50% in OrcaSlicer filament cooling settings, disable auxiliary fan, and raise nozzle printing temperature to 245°C.

faq.question: Can the Bambu Lab A1 Mini's 80°C bed temperature adequately adhere Overture PETG?
faq.answer: Yes, running the heatbed at its maximum 80°C target provides sufficient glass transition thermal energy for Overture PETG adhesion on the textured PEI plate.

faq.question: Does Overture PETG require a hardened steel nozzle on the A1 Mini?
faq.answer: No, standard Overture PETG is non-abrasive and can be run indefinitely through the stock stainless steel nozzle without premature orifice wear.

faq.question: Why is a release agent necessary on the textured PEI plate for PETG?
faq.answer: PETG chemically fuses to bare PEI surfaces; using a thin coat of glue stick acts as a release barrier to prevent tearing chunks of PEI coating off the plate during part removal.

faq.question: What is the recommended flow ratio and pressure advance calibration value?
faq.answer: Start with a flow ratio of 0.95 to 0.97 in OrcaSlicer, with typical Pressure Advance (PA) calibrated around 0.035 to 0.045 s for direct drive extrusion with this material.
